findings.description: The migration forbids automatic rollback to a JSON-only binary, but the preserved release workflow captures the previously released backend image and automatically redeploys it after deployment or smoke failure. The plan does not specify how the first Identity migration establishes a compatible captured rollback target or prevents the existing automatic rollback from selecting the JSON-only predecessor. Merely documenting a compatible image does not change that workflow. Once source credentials are removed, this rollback cannot preserve account/session authority.

findings.recommendation: Specify an executable, gate-preserving transition sequence that establishes and verifies the compatible rollback target before import commitment. Choose an explicit compatibility rollout or an audited migration-aware rollback selection/guard, identify the affected implementation paths, and rehearse failure after import commit, source cleanup, and resumed auth writes through the actual release rollback mechanism.

findings.description: The external-Google-email flow has no fully specified transition from mailbox verification to signed-in completion. Provider completion returns verify_mailbox, while email verification declares provider_mailbox_verified and permits session creation only for signed_in. The only provider completion request requires the original one-use handoff code, whose lifetime is at most 60 seconds, whereas mailbox verification may take up to ten minutes. The contracts do not identify a finalizing response or a replacement continuation authority, so clients cannot implement this journey consistently after the original handoff expires or is consumed.
evidence: specs/022-modern-auth/plan.md:94 requires mailbox proof before durable creation for new Google third-party addresses.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:33 lists provider_mailbox_verified and states that only signed_in may create a session.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:42 requires handoff_code for provider completion; line 48 makes it one-use and at most 60 seconds.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:56 lists verify_mailbox as a provider completion outcome.
specs/022-modern-auth/data-model.md:10-12 defines mailbox-required attempts, 60-second handoffs, and ten-minute challenges without an explicit continuation transition.
findings.recommendation: Define the exact mailbox-required completion edge and matching web/native response contract. For example, consume the callback handoff when entering the client-bound mailbox-required state, then let successful mailbox verification atomically finalize that same staged provider attempt and return signed_in. Alternatively, specify a bounded replacement continuation proof and its endpoint. Preserve the original callback evidence, client binding, attempt lifetime, uniqueness checks, and one-use semantics.
